title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs' (deuxième mouture), a programme for a tame or combinatorial topology of 'figures'. The page is read in that framework, and the meanings of the symbols are inferred from how they are used. 𝓕 is a set of figures. F' ≤ F is inclusion or sub-figure. F' ≪ F is a stronger relation, probably 'F' is a sub-figure built from pieces of F'. comb(F) is the set of combinatorial pieces (cells or strata) of F. x ∥ F' appears to mean that x and F' are 'separated' (disjoint, or not meeting in the open sense).

Page 84 proved that, for F' ≪ F, three conditions are equivalent: (i) a criterion checked with axiom At 13; (ii) no x in comb(F) satisfies x ∥ F', i.e. F' is 'dense' in F; (iii) F' is maximal among F'' with F' ≤ F'' ≪ F.

Page 85, Definition: when these conditions hold, F' is a subdivision of F, and F is a surdivision or regroupement of F'. This is written F' ≼ F.

Proposition 1: ≼ is an order relation. Reflexivity is clear. For transitivity, suppose G ∥ F''. Then F'' ≼ F' gives G ∥ F', and F' ≼ F gives G ∥ F. This uses the reformulation 'every G separated from the subdivision is separated from F'.

Proposition 2 (base change): suppose G ≤ F, and F'_G = F'|G ≪ G is the induced figure. If F' ≼ F, then F'_G ≼ G. Proof: take x in comb(G) and suppose x ∥ F'_G. The lemma on p. 82 then gives x ∥ F', which contradicts F' ≼ F.

Corollary 1 (locality): let F' ≪ F, and let F_i ≤ F with Sup F_i = F. Put F'_i = F'|F_i. Then F' ≼ F if and only if F'_i ≼ F_i for all i. Necessity follows from Proposition 2. Sufficiency is shown on p. 86 using comb F = ∪ comb F_i.

The margin adds a sharpened transitivity: if F'' ≪ F' ≪ F, then F'' ≼ F ⇔ (F'' ≼ F' and F' ≼ F).

The page belongs to the build-up toward gluing of subdivisions (Cor. 2) and Th. 14 on p. 86. Th. 14 says a subdivision of a sub-figure G ≤ F extends to a subdivision of F. That is the axiomatic analogue of extending a triangulation or cell decomposition compatibly with a given subcomplex, as in PL topology and o-minimal cell decomposition.
errors: Purely logical slips in the written proof of Proposition 2, apparently caused by a negation bar that was lost or not written. 'il suffit de voir que pour x ∈ comb(G), on a x ∥ F'_G' must mean x NOT ∥ F'_G. The rest of the argument, 'mais si on avait x ∥ F'_G …', is a proof by contradiction that only makes sense with the negated claim.

The definition uses criterion (ii), stated with x ∈ comb(F). The transitivity proof instead uses the form 'for all G ∈ 𝓕, G ∥ F'' ⇒ G ∥ F'. Their equivalence is implicitly taken from the lemma or remark on pp. 82–84. This is a small gap, not an error.
The margin claim F'' ≼ F ⇒ F'' ≼ F' needs 'G ∥ F ⇒ G ∥ F'' whenever F' ≪ F (monotonicity of separation). That is plausible but not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Definition of subdivision F' ≼ F as a 'dense', maximal finer sub-figure, characterised by separation from cells
ideas.modern_name: subdivision / refinement of stratifications or cell decompositions (PL and o-minimal subdivision)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman); o-minimal cell decompositions (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5; the 1986 axiomatic details are unpublished

ideas.what: Subdivisions are stable under restriction to sub-figures and are local for coverings (Sup F_i = F), leading to gluing of subdivisions
ideas.modern_name: subdivisions form a sheaf/stack-like local notion; restriction of subdivisions to subcomplexes

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine order-theoretic and locality properties of subdivisions inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame topology. The overall programme is of historical interest, and it is known to exist in outline from the Esquisse. Nothing on this page goes beyond standard facts about subdivisions.
transcription_corrections: In Proposition 2: 'il suffit de voir que si pour x ∈ comb(G), on a x ∥ F'_G' should read '…on n'a pas x ∥ F'_G' (negated separation).
In the Corollary, 'la restriction de F_i [?] induite' is presumably 'la restriction de F' à F_i' (the induced figure F'|F_i).
On the next page, 'prouvons qu'on peut avoir x ∥ F'' should be 'qu'on ne peut avoir x ∥ F''.
Margin: 'Si F' ≃ F … complicateur' is probably a remark that ≼ need not be antisymmetric up to isomorphism, or that an alternative definition would be more complicated. The reading is uncertain.
In the statement 'Si F' ≼ F, alors F'_G ≼ G', the image shows F'_G subscripted, consistent with the diagram F'_G ≪ G.
